item.title: Embassy vs RTIC vs esp-hal in 2026: Which Async Runtime Should Run Your Embedded Rust?
item.description: Firmware written with a bare superloop plus a handful of interrupt handlers has a predictable failure mode: at 40 MHz everything works, and at 400 kHz of event traffic two handlers start corrupting the same state machine. The classic fix — a real-time operating system — costs you a scheduler tick, a heap, and a debugger workflow that no longer matches the silicon. Rust’s answer is different: keep the single stack, drop the RTOS, and get concurrency from async plus compile-time priority analysis.
